hints: Spinner 1 has 5 sides: $1, 1, 1, 2, 3$. Spinner 2 has 3 sides: $1, 2, 3$. There are $5 \times 3 = 15$ equally likely outcomes.
Calculate the product of the numbers for each of the 15 outcomes.
Count the frequency of each score out of 15 to form the probability distribution table.
walkthrough:
List all 15 outcomes and their products (score $X$):
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
\text{Spinner 1} \setminus \text{Spinner 2} & 1 & 2 & 3 \\
\hline
1 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\
1 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\
1 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\
2 & 2 & 4 & 6 \\
3 & 3 & 6 & 9 \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

Count the frequency and calculate the probability for each distinct score $x$:
$$\begin{array}{lcl}
\mathrm{P}(X = 1) &=& \frac{3}{15} \\
\mathrm{P}(X = 2) &=& \frac{4}{15} \\
\mathrm{P}(X = 3) &=& \frac{4}{15} \\
\mathrm{P}(X = 4) &=& \frac{1}{15} \\
\mathrm{P}(X = 6) &=& \frac{2}{15} \\
\mathrm{P}(X = 9) &=& \frac{1}{15}
\end{array}$$

Construct the probability distribution table:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline x & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 6 & 9 \\ \hline \mathrm{P}(X = x) & \frac{3}{15} & \frac{4}{15} & \frac{4}{15} & \frac{1}{15} & \frac{2}{15} & \frac{1}{15} \\ \hline \end{array}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Two spinners are spun: Spinner 1 has sides $(1, 1, 1, 2, 3)$ and Spinner 2 has sides $(1, 2, 3)$. The score $X$ is the product of the two numbers.

Step 1: Determine the total number of outcomes.
Spinner 1 has 5 equally likely sides and Spinner 2 has 3 equally likely sides, so there are $5 \times 3 = 15$ equally likely pairs.

Step 2: Calculate the product for all 15 pairs:
- Side 1 from Spinner 1 (occurs 3 times):
  $1 \times 1 = 1$ (3 times)
  $1 \times 2 = 2$ (3 times)
  $1 \times 3 = 3$ (3 times)
- Side 2 from Spinner 1 (occurs 1 time):
  $2 \times 1 = 2$ (1 time)
  $2 \times 2 = 4$ (1 time)
  $2 \times 3 = 6$ (1 time)
- Side 3 from Spinner 1 (occurs 1 time):
  $3 \times 1 = 3$ (1 time)
  $3 \times 2 = 6$ (1 time)
  $3 \times 3 = 9$ (1 time)

Step 3: Collect frequencies for each unique product:
- Product 1: 3 times $\implies \mathrm{P}(X = 1) = \frac{3}{15}$
- Product 2: $3 + 1 = 4$ times $\implies \mathrm{P}(X = 2) = \frac{4}{15}$
- Product 3: $3 + 1 = 4$ times $\implies \mathrm{P}(X = 3) = \frac{4}{15}$
- Product 4: 1 time $\implies \mathrm{P}(X = 4) = \frac{1}{15}$
- Product 6: $1 + 1 = 2$ times $\implies \mathrm{P}(X = 6) = \frac{2}{15}$
- Product 9: 1 time $\implies \mathrm{P}(X = 9) = \frac{1}{15}$

Step 4: Present in the distribution table:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline x & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 6 & 9 \\ \hline \mathrm{P}(X = x) & \frac{3}{15} & \frac{4}{15} & \frac{4}{15} & \frac{1}{15} & \frac{2}{15} & \frac{1}{15} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

hints: Calculate the mean using $\mathrm{E}(X) = \sum x \,\mathrm{P}(X = x)$.
Use the variance formula $\operatorname{Var}(X) = \mathrm{E}(X^2) - [\mathrm{E}(X)]^2$ to find the variance.
teacher_walkthrough: We calculate the mean $\mathrm{E}(X)$ and variance $\operatorname{Var}(X)$ of the score from the distribution in part (i).

Step 3: Compute $\operatorname{Var}(X) = \mathrm{E}(X^2) - [\mathrm{E}(X)]^2$:
$$\operatorname{Var}(X) = \frac{224}{15} - (3.2)^2 = \frac{224}{15} - 10.24 = \frac{224}{15} - \frac{256}{25}$$
Using a common denominator of 75:
$$\operatorname{Var}(X) = \frac{1120 - 768}{75} = \frac{352}{75} \approx 4.6933$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $\operatorname{Var}(X) = 4.69$ (or exact fraction $\frac{352}{75}$).

hints: Use the mean score found in part (ii): $\mathrm{E}(X) = 3.2$.
Identify all score values strictly greater than $3.2$: $x = 4, 6, 9$.
Add their probabilities from the table: $\mathrm{P}(X = 4) + \mathrm{P}(X = 6) + \mathrm{P}(X = 9)$.
walkthrough:
Identify scores greater than the mean score $\mathrm{E}(X) = 3.2$:
$$\text{Scores with } x > 3.2 \implies x \in \{4, 6, 9\}$$

Sum the probabilities for these scores from the distribution table:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 3.2) = \mathrm{P}(X = 4) + \mathrm{P}(X = 6) + \mathrm{P}(X = 9)$$
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 3.2) = \frac{1}{15} + \frac{2}{15} + \frac{1}{15} = \frac{4}{15} \approx 0.267$$
teacher_walkthrough: We need to find the probability that the score is strictly greater than the mean score found in part (ii).

Step 1: State the mean score from part (ii):
$$\text{Mean} = 3.2$$

Step 2: Identify the outcomes that are strictly greater than $3.2$:
The possible scores in our distribution are $1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9$. The scores exceeding $3.2$ are $4, 6,$ and $9$.

Step 3: Sum the corresponding probabilities from the table in part (i):
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 3.2) = \mathrm{P}(X = 4) + \mathrm{P}(X = 6) + \mathrm{P}(X = 9)$$
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 3.2) = \frac{1}{15} + \frac{2}{15} + \frac{1}{15} = \frac{4}{15} \approx 0.267$$
